Class Record

java.lang.Object
org.cobol4j.Record
public final class Record extends Object
A COBOL record: a named, hierarchical group of fields backed by a byte buffer.

The byte buffer IS the data — just like COBOL. Fields are views over byte ranges, with encoding/decoding governed by their PIC clause and Usage. REDEFINES creates alternate views over the same bytes. OCCURS creates indexed views at computed offsets.

Usage — define a record, then use it: 

Record customer = Record.define("CUSTOMER-RECORD")
    .group("CUST-NAME", name -> name
        .pic("FIRST-NAME",  "X(20)")
        .pic("LAST-NAME",   "X(25)"))
    .pic("CUST-BALANCE", "S9(7)V99").comp3()
    .pic("CUST-STATUS", "X")
        .value88("ACTIVE",   "A")
        .value88("INACTIVE", "I")
    .build();

customer.move("FIRST-NAME", "JOHN");
customer.move("CUST-BALANCE", new BigDecimal("12345.67"));
if (customer.is("ACTIVE")) { ... }

    • moveSubstring

      public Record moveSubstring(String fieldName, int position, int length, String value)
      Reference modification on the receiving side — write into a substring of a field. Position is 1-based (COBOL style). MOVE "ABC" TO FIELD(5:3) writes "ABC" into positions 5-7 of FIELD.

    • field

      public Field field(String fieldName)
      Get a live Field reference — a by-reference handle into this record's buffer. The Field can be stored, passed to methods, and used for GIVING, SEARCH, SORT.

    • initialize

      public Record initialize()
      INITIALIZE — reset all elementary fields to type-appropriate defaults. Alphanumeric/alphabetic → SPACES, numeric → ZEROS. Recurses through group items. Skips FILLER fields.
